extracted.intended_audience: USPTO management, auditors, oversight bodies, and internal program managers (patent and trademark organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, criteria, and program requirements used by the USPTO (and its auditors) to assess financial/internal controls, improper payments, facility/energy stewardship, and examiner/training programs. Covers audit standards considered, payment-control processes, customer experience metrics, and detailed training curricula for patent and trademark examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards considered in IT general controls audit
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing our procedures, we considered DOC and USPTO policies and various Federal standards and guidance such as (1) GAO’s Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government, dated September 2014, (2) GAO’s Federal Information System Controls Audit Manual, dated February 2009, (3) NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, and (4) NIST Special Publication 800-34 Rev. 1, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to the nature of IT general controls, certain information has been omitted from the public report; a separate limited distribution IT report includes specific findings, the criteria used, cause analysis, and recommendations. Auditors consider federal control frameworks (GAO, NIST) when evaluating IT general controls, configuration/patch management, access/distribution controls, and integrity of application controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Payments identification and reporting (IPIA/IPERA/IPERIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPIA of 2002, as amended by IPERA (2010) and IPERIA (2012), requires agencies to periodically review all programs and activities to identify those susceptible to significant improper payments, take multiple actions when programs are identified as susceptible, and annually report information on improper payments monitoring and minimization efforts. OMB Circular A-123, Appendix C, provides guidance to comply with these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document program reviews, actions taken to reduce improper payments, and annual reporting. The USPTO reported it has not identified any programs susceptible to significant improper payments for FY 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual risk assessment of programs and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of all programs and activities that the USPTO administers is performed annually to assist in identifying, reporting, and/or preventing erroneous or improper payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO completes an annual improper payments risk assessment covering all programs/activities as required by OMB Circular A-123, Appendix C; these assessments include the control and procurement environment. Every three years the assessment includes a review of internal controls over disbursement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling requirement for improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical sampling is used to estimate the improper payment rate for programs and activities that are susceptible to significant improper payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency has no programs susceptible to significant improper payments, statistical sampling to estimate improper payment rates is not required; USPTO did not conduct statistical sampling in FY 2016 because no risk-susceptible programs were identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payments reporting: reduction outlook, root causes, corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When programs/activities are identified as susceptible to significant improper payments, agencies must present an improper payment reduction outlook, root cause analyses, and corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the USPTO identified no risk-susceptible programs in FY 2016, it did not present a reduction outlook, root cause analyses, or corrective actions for programs in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFO accountability for improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s CFO has responsibility for establishing policies and procedures for assessing USPTO and program risks of improper payments, taking actions to reduce improper payments, and reporting the results to management for oversight and other actions as deemed appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFO has designated the Deputy CFO to oversee initiatives related to reducing improper payments; describe roles and oversight responsibilities for accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment recapture audits determined by cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment recapture audits may be conducted to recapture overpayments, but agencies should evaluate whether recapture audits are cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO does not currently conduct recapture audits because prior recapture audit activity did not yield meaningful results; therefore payment recapture rates and related metrics are not presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpayments tracking and reporting outside recapture audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and report overpayments identified and overpayments verified as recaptured through sources other than payment recapture audits, including current-year, prior-year, and cumulative totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables summarizing amounts identified for recapture and amounts recaptured, broken out by current year/prior years and by source (post-payment reviews, audits, vendor reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Pay Initiative vendor validation processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate IPERIA-listed Do Not Pay databases and other appropriate sources into business processes to prevent improper payments, including periodic vendor eligibility validation and post-payment screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO has incorporated the SSA Death Master File and GSA’s Excluded Parties List System/SAM; implemented monthly batch post-payment screening of a subset of payments; continuous monitoring of a subset of active vendor records; results should be used to maintain vendor records and reduce improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and minimization processes for improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify improper payments through post-payment reviews, contract closeout reviews, credit memos/refunds, returned electronic payments, and monthly inquiries with business units; implement process improvements to reduce erroneous payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include keeping a master file for vendor payment assignments accessible to technicians and approvers, periodic reminders to monitor assignments, and reporting procedures to senior management and Department of Commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeze the Footprint reporting metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and report facility square footage baseline and year-over-baseline changes (Freeze the Footprint Baseline Comparison) and operations & maintenance costs for direct lease buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report square footage (in millions of SF) for baseline and changes by fiscal year, and report operating cost changes (dollars in millions) for direct lease buildings to demonstrate footprint management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy Star building performance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Energy Star award requires attaining strict building performance standards: Energy Star buildings use less energy, cost less to operate, produce fewer greenhouse gas emissions and perform better than 75 percent of similar office buildings nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use industry-recognized benchmarks and performance comparisons to qualify for awards and to measure building energy efficiency improvements (e.g., LED retrofits, T-8 to T-8 replacements, renewable energy credits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste diversion targets and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure waste diversion as a percentage of total waste stream and compare to government targets (e.g., president’s goal of 50 percent minimum waste diversion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report diversion percentage annually and document supporting programs (e.g., Office Supply Exchange) and outreach (Green Fair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace safety and employee viewpoint survey metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Employee Viewpoint Survey metrics (e.g., percent of employees who believe they are sufficiently protected from health and safety hazards; percent who believe the agency prepared them for potential security threats) and compare to government-wide averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentages and benchmarking to show relative performance and identify areas needing improvement (e.g., lighting, noise, cleanliness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety program requirements for warehouse facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive safety program should include safety and occupational health training, job orientation safety training, mishap reporting and abatement actions, and site familiarization safety training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate additional safety activities (e.g., blood drives) and report program outcomes and participation to demonstrate program reach and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: File repository records management compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer or dispose of file repository records in accordance with federal regulations and guidelines to be better stewards of records management and reduce space holdings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a multi-year initiative with documented compliance to federal records schedules and disposal/transfer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training program comprehensive content for patent examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiner training must provide extensive legal, technical, and IT systems training, including initial legal training, systems training, examination practice and procedure, technology-specific legal and technical training, and systems training when new IT systems are deployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should be reviewed and evaluated on an ongoing basis to ensure coursework reflects developments and changes in the industry and examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-inventor-to-file AIA training phased approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on first-inventor-to-file delivered in three phases: (1) introductory overview training with videos, (2) comprehensive training session with videos, and (3) a hands-on workshop designed to introduce examiners to situations that may arise in prosecution; supplemented by a computer-based training library and an internal website for lecture materials and FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mixed delivery methods (in-person, WebEx, computer-based) and targeted hands-on workshops to address statutory changes and nuanced topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Patent Training Academy curricula and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Two patent examiner training programs exist: an Intellectual Property Experienced Examiner Training and an entry-level two-phased 12-month new examiner program. Curricula include USPC and CPC classification, searching (classification, text), claim interpretation, advanced text searching, writing an effective examiner’s answer, appeal procedure and practice, technology-specific introductions, automation training (specialized applications and multiple search systems), and life skills training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specialized automation classes, multiple search systems training (STN, Dialog), and include appeal procedure practice (Appeal Conference and Pre-Conference). Ensure experienced and entry-level curricula cover overlapping legal/procedural and technical competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Development Plan (IDP) and life skills training
rubrics_metrics.description: Each examiner receives an IDP composed of formal training courses, development assignments, and on-the-job training to assist through the first 12 months and beyond. Life skills training includes time management, ethics, stress management, balancing quality and production, professionalism, benefits/financial planning, and diversity/conflict negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IDPs to track competency acquisition and continued development after Academy graduation; align life skills training to help examiners balance quality and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized and continuing patent education programs (PETTP, SEE, Continuing Education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special programs include PETTP (industry/academic experts presenting state-of-the-art topics), SEE (site experience education visits to innovation sites), and Continuing Education Series to enhance technical and legal knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage external subject-matter experts, site visits to industry/academic innovators, and ongoing courses (including non-duty hour programs) to maintain examiner technical currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examining attorney initial training and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks trains newly hired examining attorneys in a classroom setting during their first seven to eight weeks, followed by integration into a law office where each attorney is mentored by a senior attorney or paired with an experienced examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign new attorneys to law offices (about 25 attorneys) with mentoring support; use online e-learning modules and live/webcast sessions developed from quality review data to cover specified topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark training content development and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark training content is developed using data from quality reviews and released as live/webcast sessions, modules, exam guides, exam notes, and guidance newsletters covering topics such as TMEP updates, ID Manual updates, ethics, evidence procedures, and topical seminars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish exam guides and exam notes and release targeted guidance to address procedural updates and common examination problems; track topics covered and training dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark law office pilot onboarding and training practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot objectives: promote engagement, camaraderie, consistent training, earlier real-world work experience, and deeper understanding of examination law. Practices include manager/mentor participation, elimination of fake files, shorter classroom training, daily real-file examination, and daily case chats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure pilot outcomes by evaluator observations: immediate feedback, real-time evaluation, unified messaging, increased responsibility, application of lessons learned, and enhanced peer discussion to reveal gray areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Experience Excellence Program metrics and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a best-in-class Customer Experience Excellence Program including baseline analysis of customer service delivery, customer journey maps, customer segmentation frameworks, customer personas, benchmarking against industry standards, and a definition of 'exceptional customer service' with proposed metrics to track progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage current customer satisfaction measures and historical data, benchmark against public/private sector best practices, and produce recommendations with proposed metrics for implementation and tracking.
